title: Why India May Accept Asian Games Medals From Mohsin Naqvi After Asia Cup Snub
excerpt: At the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, the medal protocol belongs to the OCA — and its Rule 66 bans podium demonstrations, meaning Indian cricketers are expected to accept medals from whoever is delegated, even ACC chief Mohsin Naqvi.
body:
• Indian cricketers are expected to accept their Asian Games medals even if the Olympic Council of Asia delegates the presentation to ACC chief Mohsin Naqvi.
  • That marks a sharp departure from the Asia Cup in Dubai, where both Indian teams twice refused to receive trophies from Naqvi.
  • The difference is protocol: OCA Rule 66 governs Asian Games victory ceremonies, and demonstrations at the podium can draw penalties up to disqualification and medal withdrawal.
  • A top Indian Olympic Association source says neither the IOA nor the BCCI can ask the OCA to exclude a particular presenter — "it's the Asian Games, not an ICC or bilateral tournament."

The same man, a different stage

If India wins a cricket medal at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, the silverware could be handed over by Mohsin Naqvi — the Pakistan Cricket Board chairman, Asian Cricket Council president and Pakistan's Federal Interior Minister whom India's cricket teams have twice refused to accept trophies from in Dubai. This time, Indian cricketers are expected to take their medals from whoever the Olympic Council of Asia nominates — even if it is Naqvi.

The shift is not about a change of stance toward Naqvi. It is about a change of jurisdiction.

What happened in Dubai

The standoff began at the 2025 Asia Cup final on September 28, 2025, at the Dubai International Stadium. India beat Pakistan by five wickets to win the title, then refused to collect the trophy and winners' medals from Naqvi, who insisted on presenting them himself as ACC chairman. India had requested that another ACC official — the Emirates Cricket Board vice-chairman was among the names floated — do the honours; Naqvi refused. The presentation ceremony was delayed by more than an hour, presenter Simon Doull eventually announced that India would not collect its awards, and Naqvi left the venue with the trophy and the winners' medals. The trophy has still not been handed over.

BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia called it "a conscious, institutional decision" and said the team had been told beforehand it would not participate in a presentation involving Naqvi. "India is fighting a war with a country, and a leader belonging to that country was supposed to hand over the trophy to us. We cannot accept a trophy from a person who represents a country that is waging a war against our country," Saikia said, adding that India would launch "a very serious and very strong protest" against Naqvi at the ICC conference in November. The BCCI maintains the trophy belongs to the ACC and should be returned via the ACC headquarters.

The episode came against the backdrop of the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025 and India's retaliatory Operation Sindoor, as well as Naqvi's anti-India social media posts. The tournament was already charged: India refused handshakes with Pakistani players, Pakistan fast bowler Haris Rauf was fined 30 percent of his match fee for a provocative 'plane crash' gesture, and Sahibzada Farhan was warned for a mock 'gunshot' celebration.

A year later, it happened again. On September 13, 2026, India's women beat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Women's Asia Cup final in Dubai — 183 for 5 against 111, built on a 129-run opening stand by Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma and 4 for 20 from Shree Charani — to win a record eighth title. Harmanpreet Kaur's team stayed away from the official presentation. The compromise: no winners' trophy was presented at all. The team held its own medal ceremony on the ground, with Saikia handing the best-fielder's medal to Nandni Sharma, before the players returned to the dressing room.

Head coach Amol Muzumdar said the decision belonged to the board: "The stand has been taken by the BCCI, and we stand by it. For us, this tournament is over. We are the champions... Now, we look forward to the Asian Games." BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla called it a collective decision and said Naqvi raised no objection. Former captain Kapil Dev, asked about the controversy on the sidelines of a golf event inauguration in Chhattisgarh, brushed it aside with a one-liner: "Tell all of them to play golf."

Why the Asian Games are different

At the Asian Games, the protocol belongs to the OCA, not the ACC — and the OCA's manual is explicit. Rule 66 on victory and medals ceremonies states that medals "shall be presented by the OCA president," who "may delegate this privilege to other members of the OCA," accompanied by the president of the international or Asian federation concerned. Crucially, the same rule states that "no kind of demonstration or commercial, political, religious or racial propaganda is permitted during the victory ceremony," and that any disrespect shown to the Games, medals, flags or certificates "will be subject to penalisation" — including disqualification, withdrawal of medals and certificates, and loss of accreditation.

In other words, a repeat of the Dubai podium snub could cost the athletes their medals. That is why a top IOA source, quoted in reporting on the protocol question, said India cannot engineer the ceremony in advance: "India can't ask OCA not to nominate Naqvi. After all, it's the Asian Games, not an ICC or bilateral tournament. Neither IOA nor BCCI can place such a request before OCA or ask it to choose or exclude a particular person. Such a request cannot be made to OCA pre-emptively."

"India can't ask OCA not to nominate Naqvi. After all, it's the Asian Games, not an ICC or bilateral tournament."

— Top IOA source, quoted in reporting on the OCA protocol question

Naqvi is already part of the cricket setup at the Games: the OCA and the Aichi-Nagoya organisers are coordinating all cricketing matters with the ACC, and the preparation of Kōrogi Sports Park — the venue for the cricket events — has been overseen by the ACC with Naqvi involved. It will fall to the OCA to decide who stands on the podium when medals are awarded.

Diaspora Angle

For the diaspora, the protocol question crystallises the tension between national sentiment and sporting discipline: the same fans who cheered the trophy snub in Dubai will be watching closely to see how Indian cricketers handle a podium where the rules leave them no room to refuse.

What's Next

Cricket at the Asian Games begins with the women's competition already underway and the men's tournament from September 24. If India medals in either, the ceremony — and whoever presents it — will answer the question the Dubai stand-offs raised. The broader BCCI-ACC dispute, meanwhile, heads to the ICC meeting in November, where the BCCI has said it will lodge a formal protest over the withheld Asia Cup trophy.
